subject: biology
question_text: Which of the following is not correct? (a) Robert Brown discovered the cell. (b) Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory. (c) Virchow explained that cells are formed from pre-existing cells. (d) A unicellular organism carries out its life activities within a single cell.

mcq_options.option_text: Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory.
Virchow explained that cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
A unicellular organism carries out its life activities within a single cell.

answer_text: (a) Robert Brown did not discover the cell. The cell was discovered by Robert Hook.
final_answer: Therefore, Robert Brown did not discover the cell.

subject: biology
question_text: What is a mesosome in a prokaryotic cell? Mention the functions that it performs.
answer_text: Mesosome is a convoluted membranous structure formed in a prokaryotic cell by the invagination of the plasma membrane. Its functions are as follows: (1) These extensions help in the synthesis of the cell wall, replication of DNA. They also help in the equal distribution of chromosomes into the daughter cells. (2) It also increases the surface area of the plasma membrane to carry out various enzymatic activities. (3) It helps in secretion processes as well as in bacterial respiration.
final_answer: Thus, mesosomes play crucial roles in prokaryotic cell functions.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of cell structure and functions.

subject: biology
question_text: How do neutral solutes move across the plasma membrane? Can the polar molecules also move across it in the same way? If not, then how are these transported across the membrane?
answer_text: Neutral molecules move across the plasma membrane by simple passive diffusion. The movement of polar molecules across the non-polar lipid bilayer requires carrier-proteins.
final_answer: Thus, neutral solutes move by diffusion while polar molecules require carrier-proteins.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of membrane transport mechanisms.

subject: biology
question_text: What are nuclear pores? State their function.
answer_text: Nuclear pores are tiny holes present in the nuclear membrane of the nucleus. They are formed by the fusion of two nuclear membranes. These holes allow specific substances to be transferred into a cell and out from it. They allow molecules such as RNA and proteins to move in both directions, between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
final_answer: Therefore, nuclear pores facilitate the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of cell structure and function.

subject: biology
question_text: Both lysosomes and vacuoles are endomembrane structures, yet they differ in terms of their functions. Comment.
answer_text: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures holding a variety of enzymes such as lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases. The purpose of lysosomes is to digest worn out cells. They are involved in the intracellular digestion of foreign food particles and microbes. Sometimes, they also act as suicidal bags. They are involved in the self digestion of cells. They are a kind of waste disposal systems of a cell. On the other hand, vacuoles are storage sacs found in cells. They might store the waste products of cells. In unicellular organisms, the food vacuole contains the consumed food particles. It also plays a role in expelling excess water and some wastes from the cell.
final_answer: Thus, lysosomes are primarily involved in digestion, while vacuoles serve as storage.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves comparison and understanding of two cell structures.

subject: biology
question_text: Describe the structure of the following with the help of labelled diagrams. (i) Nucleus (ii) Centrosome

question_image.description: Labelled diagrams of the nucleus and centrosome showing their structures.

answer_text: The nucleus controls all the cellular activities of the cell. It is spherical in shape. It is composed of the following structures: Nuclear membrane: It is a double membrane separating the contents of the nucleus from the cytoplasm. The narrow space between the two membranes is called the perinuclear space. Nuclear membrane has tiny holes called nuclear pores. These holes allow specific substances to be transferred into a cell and out from it. Nucleoplasm/Nuclear matrix: It is a homogenous granular fluid present inside the nucleus. It contains the nucleolus and chromatin. Nucleolus is a spherical structure that is not bound by any membrane. It is rich in protein and RNA molecules, and is the site for ribosome formation. Chromatin is an entangled mass of thread-like structures. It contains DNA and some basic proteins called histones. Centrosome consists of two cylindrical structures called centrioles. Centrioles lie perpendicular to each other. Each has a cartwheel-like organisation. A centriole is made up of microtubule triplets that are evenly spaced in a ring. The adjacent triplets are linked together. There is a proteinaceous hub in the central part of a centriole. The hub is connected to the triplets via radial spokes. These centrioles help in organising the spindle fibres and astral rays during cell division. They form the basal body of cilia and flagella.
final_answer: Thus, the nucleus and centrosome are essential structures with distinct functions in the cell.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires detailed understanding and description of two complex structures.

subject: biology
question_text: Define sub-metacentric, acrocentric, and telocentric chromosomes.

question_image.description: Diagrams illustrating different types of chromosomes: sub-metacentric, acrocentric, and telocentric.

answer_text: A sub-metacentric chromosome has the centromere slightly away from the middle, making one arm longer than the other. An acrocentric chromosome has the centromere close to one end, resulting in one very long arm and one very short arm. A telocentric chromosome has the centromere at one terminal end.
final_answer: Thus, these definitions categorize chromosomes based on the position of their centromeres.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of chromosome structure and definitions.
